reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) concerns different alloy systems (FCC-based HEAs with L12 precipitates, not BCC refractory HEAs with B2 precipitates) and does not address dynamic strain hardening, adiabatic shear banding, or the specific strength/ductility predictions for HfZrTiTa0.53. The key premises thus lack specific prior support.
premises: Aging at ~700°C can produce a uniform dispersion of nanoscale ordered precipitates in refractory HEAs
Nanoscale precipitates enhance dynamic strain hardening by acting as obstacles to dislocation motion
Enhanced strain hardening promotes uniform plastic deformation and delays adiabatic shear band formation
The intervention will improve dynamic strength by ~20% and fracture strain from 13.5% to 18–20%
These improvements apply under adiabatic SHPB conditions at 1000–3000 s⁻¹
